scienceGoal: Measure heat flowing from the Moon's interior
nightBehaviour: Powers down — too cold to drill, needs heater to survive
funFact: LISTER was designed by Honeybee Robotics to drill up to 3 metres into regolith

scienceGoal: Bounce laser light back to orbiting spacecraft for precise ranging
nightBehaviour: Sleeps peacefully — passive optics need no power and work for decades
funFact: The LRA is just 8 glass prisms in an aluminium hemisphere. No electronics, no power, works forever

scienceGoal: Test how lunar dust sticks to different materials
nightBehaviour: Shivers in the cold — dust still clings to surfaces even at night
funFact: Lunar dust is electrostatically charged and sticks to everything — it was one of the biggest complaints from Apollo astronauts

scienceGoal: Detect water vapour and other volatiles at the surface
nightBehaviour: Hibernates — the mass spectrometer needs significant power to ionise molecules
funFact: MSolo flew on IM-2 to the south pole to sniff for water ice near Shackleton crater

scienceGoal: Film the landing plume and measure how it moves regolith
nightBehaviour: Saves battery — cameras go to sleep mode but stay warm enough for the electronics
funFact: SCALPSS uses camera technology from the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover

scienceGoal: Capture regolith samples using pneumatic suction
nightBehaviour: Locks down — the sample container seals to protect its precious cargo
funFact: PlanetVac was originally tested on Mauna Kea, Hawai'i, using volcanic soil as a Moon stand-in
